We are so proud to announce that we have won Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Setting of the Year 2025!
“… The holistic understanding of child development, neuroscience and social and emotional wellbeing are exemplary!”
We are absolutely delighted to share that Edgeborough has been awarded Flagship School Status by the Learning Skills Trust — becoming the very first school to receive this prestigious recognition.
This award celebrates the school’s exemplary practice under the PSB Framework, unwavering commitment to excellence, strong leadership in supporting pupil learning and staff development, and its contribution as a leading example of best practice across the Trust.
Welcome to Edgeborough
Welcome to Edgeborough School – a co-educational, independent Prep School for pupils aged 2–13 in Farnham, Surrey.
Edgeborough is a vibrant, nurturing community set within 50 acres in the beautiful Surrey Hills. As one of the leading independent school Surrey families choose, our spacious grounds provide endless opportunities for adventure, discovery and meaningful learning, both inside and outside the classroom.
At Edgeborough, we balance the joy of childhood with high aspirations, inspiring pupils to flourish academically, socially and emotionally. As a private school Surrey parents trust, we place kindness, respect and curiosity at the heart of everything we do. Our close partnership with Charterhouse further enriches pupils’ experiences and opens exciting pathways for the future.
We warmly invite you to visit and experience what makes Edgeborough such a special place to learn and grow.
“ Inclusive,ambitious, justthe right balanceof traditional andmodern – and ahuge amount offun. ”

Discover Edgeborough at our Open Mornings
Edgeborough holds Open Mornings throughout the year. These give the opportunity to meet our Head, tour the school with our Prep School guides and speak to teachers and pupils. We look forward to welcoming you to Edgeborough School.
Our next Open Morning – Friday 2nd October 2026​
If you have any queries please contact our Head of Admissions, Debbie Tully admissions@edgeborough.co.uk. or call us on 01252 792495.
From the age of 2, children may join our happy and flourishing Nursery family and become a part of a supportive, enriching and caring community. In the academic year within which the child turns 4 years of age, they progress to our Pre-School community.
Beyond the classrooms and woodland garden, Edgeborough’s exceptional grounds gift the children with daily adventures and the unrivalled opportunity to be at one with the natural world and to learn from it. Woodland walks are a daily occurrence, and provide vital sensory stimuli, physical exertion and learning opportunity through seasonal cycles and change. For the Pre-School children magic awaits them in our weekly Forest School sessions. Emphasis is given to helping each child develop in the EYFS’s core areas of learning; communication, physical development and their personal, social and emotional development.
Joining Edgeborough School at age 7, entering Year 3, marks an exciting step in a child’s educational journey where they become part of a dynamic and supportive learning community. At this pivotal stage, pupils are introduced to a more structured curriculum that balances academic rigor with creative exploration, fostering both intellectual and personal growth. Edgeborough’s experienced and dedicated teaching staff are committed to nurturing each child’s unique abilities, ensuring a personalised learning experience that caters to individual strengths and areas for development. The school’s vibrant extracurricular program, which includes sports, arts, and diverse club activities, complements classroom learning, encouraging pupils to discover and pursue their passions.
For more information, please contact our Head of Admissions, Debbie Tully admissions@edgeborough.co.uk, or call us on 01252 792495.
View more information about our Year 3
Joining Edgeborough School at age 11, for Years 7 and 8, offers a unique opportunity for pupils to be expertly prepared for their transition to prestigious destination schools. In these crucial two years, Edgeborough provides a tailored educational experience that focuses on academic excellence, personal growth, and readiness for entrance exams and interviews. The curriculum is designed to challenge and engage pupils, nurturing critical thinking and independent learning skills that are essential for success in senior schools. With a team of experienced educators, pupils receive personalised guidance and support tailored to their unique aspirations and capabilities, ensuring they are well-equipped to excel in their chosen paths. The school’s comprehensive program extends beyond academics, with a wide range of extracurricular activities that foster leadership, teamwork, and creativity. Edgeborough’s strong network and reputation with top senior schools offer pupils valuable opportunities and insights into various school options. Parents can be confident that Edgeborough provides not just an academic bridge, but a holistic preparation for their child’s successful transition to the next stage of their educational journey.
For more information, please contact our Head of Admissions, Debbie Tully admissions@edgeborough.co.uk, or call us on 01252 792495.

We promote creativity by making it as interesting and exciting as possible and by incorporating it into our extremely rich arts curriculum.

Educational Partnerships
In academic year 2023-2024 Edgeborough School worked in partnership with four state schools across six events, involving 247 state school pupils and 133 Edgeborough pupils. The initiatives involved pupils from Year 2 to Year 6 across six subject areas.
Focus has been on providing specialist teaching which has included Edgeborough staff and external professionals and which have taken place both on site at Edgeborough, as well as off site at a National Trust property, a crucial part in promoting opportunities for increasing state school pupils cultural capital.

The Arts are a vital part of school life at Edgeborough and our pupils have the opportunity to express themselves creatively though a huge variety of art and design classes.
We promote creativity by making it as interesting and exciting as possible and by incorporating it into our very rich curriculum.
This creative subject serves to build resilience in pupils as they learn from their mistakes and solve problems as they work through a project both individually and as a team.
All of our teachers are subject matter experts, and are often assisted by visiting artists.
The Art Department at Edgeborough aims to offer a creative and supportive learning environment for all pupils regardless of their natural ability.

Our Nursery & Pre-School welcomes children aged 2+
Nursery and Pre-School children experience a caring and stimulating environment whilst being an integral part of the school, sharing specialist French and PE teachers and the beautiful school grounds, although situated in their own exclusive house and gardens.
Based in Farnham in Surrey, the Nursery & Pre-School provides a secure and relaxed environment for children to begin their school life.
It is in our Nursery and Pre-School that your child’s Edgeborough adventure takes flight. From the age of 2, children may join our happy and flourishing Nursery family and become a part of a supportive, enriching and caring community. In the academic year within which the child turns 4 years of age, they progress to our Pre-School community.
The Nursery Day is built around active, rich play; eager, sensory exploration and authentic, purposeful routine. Structure is offered through key points of the day, including shared reading sessions, songs, lunch, walks and snacks. In essence, the environment offers an arena within which staff can follow the child, play alongside them, structure their learning and expand their interactions with friends.
Quite simply, no day is the same and whilst common features might be shared, the children, staff and Mother Nature bring wonderful uniqueness to daily content and the journey travelled by the children.
Nursery children start with a minimum of two morning sessions but many will stay for longer and enjoy lunches at school and the afternoon session. For children in the Pre-School, session bookings generally increase over the course of the school year in preparation for Reception. Children can attend any number of sessions in both the Nursery and the Pre-School, depending on availability.
Sessions are booked in advance of each term. Should the required session be oversubscribed, preference will be given to children who are entering the Pre-Prep the following September.
Session times (Term time only)
Children have the opportunity to attend Ballet, Tap and Tennis lessons during the Nursery day which are booked with the coaches directly.
Our Nursery building is homely, spacious and offers enviable freedom to the children. Both indoors and out, we have developed a neutrally calm space which provides considered enrichment and learning for the child.
Beyond the classrooms and woodland garden, Edgeborough’s exceptional grounds gift the children with daily adventures and the unrivalled opportunity to be at one with the natural world and to learn from it. Woodland walks are a daily occurrence, and provide vital sensory stimuli, physical exertion and learning opportunity through seasonal cycles and change. For the Pre-School children magic awaits them in our weekly Forest School sessions.
All children are special and we direct time and care towards offering them a wide range of open-ended resources and play engagements which reflect their interests and offer the potential for creative, challenging and collaborative play.
Emphasis is given to helping each child develop in the EYFS’s core areas of learning; communication, physical development and their personal, social and emotional development.
Our commitment is to ensure that each child thrives and flourishes within our nurturing embrace. Our staff hold the magic of childhood in their souls and carry great care and love for the child in their hearts. We offer an environment where the child is supported by highly experienced staff who guide learning through play and targeted activity, allowing each child to explore and grow at their own pace.
For children to flourish, to learn and to embrace all that Edgeborough has to offer, we prioritise relationships and see our community as one big family, where staff, parents and children know one another, trust one another and work together towards a shared objective, the happiness of the child. Together, we form an unbeatable team dedicated to ensuring the most magical start to your child’s education. Regular communication and active involvement are encouraged, as we build lasting bonds that support your child’s journey.

The Governors
Edgeborough joined the Charterhouse family of schools (Registered Charity 312054) on 1st August 2021. The Governing Body of Charterhouse School has responsibility for both schools, but the schools are run independently, retaining their own identity, name, and ethos, as well as their day-to-day operational autonomy.
The Edgeborough School Committee has been established to oversee the day to day running of Edgeborough. This Committee reports into the main Governing Body.
Members of the Governing Body
Kwaku Awuku-Asabre, BSc, Dip.Law
Kwaku is a Barrister at Matrix Chambers, London. He is an Old Carthusian who studied Economics and Philosophy at LSE. Before pursuing a career in the law, Kwaku worked in London as a fixed income analyst at Bank of America Merrill Lynch. Outside court, Kwaku has undertaken disclosure work for the Government Legal Department in relation to both the Grenfell Tower and Cyprus Colonial Litigation disclosure projects.
Mr Barnes is the Head of Governance and Compliance at RSAcademics. He is an Old Carthusian and alumnus of the University of Oxford. Durell sits on the Nominations and Governance Committee, Edgeborough School Committee, Windlesham School Committee and is Chair of the Education Committee.
Mark Bishop, BA, MA, MBA (Chair)
Mark Bishop was educated at Charterhouse before graduating from St Edmund Hall, Oxford in 1984, He began his teaching career at the Royal Grammar School, Guildford before becoming the Deputy Headmaster at Caterham School. In 1996 he was appointed Headmaster of Trinity School, Croydon, part of the Whitgift Foundation. After 10 years of headship, he became the Chief Executive of Perrett Laver, a global Executive Search company before returning to the world of schools as the High School Principal and Executive Headmaster of YK Pao School, Shanghai, one of China’s leading international schools. Mark has been a Governor of several independent schools and for many years was an Independent Schools’ Inspector in the UK. Mark joined the Governing body in September 2023 and was elected Chair from March 2024.
Stephen Browne, MA, MBA, PGCE, MCSI
A former member of the teaching staff at Charterhouse School, Stephen spent 20 years in private client and charity investment management, mostly as a director and shareholder of Waverton Investment Management. He left the industry at the end of 2022 to join technology start-up company Devyce as Chief Financial Officer. A Cambridge University graduate, Stephen began his career teaching Latin and French at Repton and subsequently Charterhouse. Stephen sits on the Education Committee and Investment Sub-Committee. He is Boarding Governor and Chair of the Charterhouse Retirement Benefit Scheme.
Michael Crawford, BSc, FCA, FSI, MBA
Michael is a Windlesham House alumnus from where he went to Wellington College and then Exeter University to study Chemistry and Law. He qualified as a chartered accountant with KPMG and went on to obtain a MBA from Cranfield University School of Management. After working as an accountant in London and Hong Kong, he embarked on a career in equity fund management working at Morgan Grenfell, Deutsch Bank and Bessemer Trust before founding Chawton Global Investors where he is currently managing partner. He returned to Windlesham as a Governor in early 2023 and joined the Charterhouse Governing Body in August 2025. Michael sits on the Committees for Finance and Business Development and Windlesham House School.
Clare Ferguson, MEng
After graduating from Oxford University with a degree in Engineering Science, Clare spent many years at NM Rothschild and Credit Suisse in credit risk, banking finance, and sales and marketing, specialising in strategy development and risk management in the precious metals markets. Clare spent nine years as a Trustee of ACS International Schools, serving as Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, the Senior Independent Director, Boarding Governor, and a member of the People Committee. She is a Trustee of the Hyde Charitable Trust, a Trustee of Action Medical Research and a Director and Trustee of Holyport College. Clare sits on the Nominations and Governance Committee and is a Director of Charterhouse International Ltd.
Helen is a solicitor and equity partner of Moore Barlow LLP. She read law at Durham university. She has nearly 20 years’ experience as a charity trustee and previously spent six years as a governor at a Godalming primary school. She lives in Godalming with her husband and two adult children and knows the local area and community very well. Helen helped lead a merger of two law firms to create a new top one hundred business and brings expertise and understanding of change management and leadership to her role as Governor. As a result of a long career representing children and adults with acquired brain injury, she also has a working knowledge of safeguarding law and the healthcare and social care sectors.
James Goldsmith, BSc, MRICS
James Goldsmith is a Director at Savills UK Limited and Head of Strategic Investment Advisory with over 25 years’ experience advising predominantly international investors in respect of their strategies for UK real estate markets. He is an Old Carthusian and studied at the University of Reading. James sits on the Finance and Business Development Committee and is Chair of the Projects and Planning Committee.
Sarah Greasley, MA(Cantab) CITP FBCS CENG FIET
Sarah Greasley was educated at St Swithun’s School, Winchester, and graduated in Mathematics from Cambridge in 1984. She has worked in technology for over 40 years, and has held senior technical executive positions at IBM, Direct Line Group and Amazon Web Services. She is a Fellow of the British Computing Society, and a Fellow of the Institute of Engineering and Technology. She served as a member of Council at St Swithun’s School from 2014-2023; and is a Trustee of the British Exploring Society. Sarah sits on the Committees for Audit, Risk and Compliance, and Projects and Planning.
Sarah is a qualified solicitor with a Jurisprudence degree from Oxford and a Post Graduate Diploma in Competition Law from Kings College, London. After training in the City of London, she spent the majority of her career working in house leading consumer, regulatory and competition legal teams at Centrica plc. In those roles she managed multi-disciplinary teams of lawyers and non-lawyers, was responsible for ley strategic business and M&A projects and regulatory investigation collaborating with the executive team throughout. Sarah sits on the committees for Audit, Risk and Compliance and the Edgeborough School Committee with particular responsibility for safeguarding.
Simon Laver, BA MA MBA
Educated at Oxford, London Business School/Dartmouth College and recent part-time studies for a BSc in Viticulture & Oenology at Plumpton College. Co-founded Perrett Laver in 2002, growing it to a leading global search firm with 21 offices and serving clients in over 70 countries, successfully transitioning to 75% employee ownership. Advised on education, science & research leadership globally, including over 500 university leadership appointments worldwide, around a third of the top 100 University Presidents/Vice-Chancellors and over 30 Russell Group VC searches. Acted as Chair/Trustee for two INGOs, one a member of DEC for which chaired the International Programme Committee. Currently chairing a government panel on UK R&D talent attraction. Recently established Gatcombe Estate Vineyard on the Isle of Wight whilst restoring the historic Georgian landscape park and gardens. Simon chairs the Windlesham House School Committee.
David is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales and was educated at Sandroyd School and Charterhouse. His professional career spanned 40 years with Saffery LLP advising charities, financial services entities and property related businesses. He served on the Management Board of the partnership and as Chairman of the firm and has held a number of professional trustee and executor positions. He continues to act as a professional consultant. David chairs the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee and is a member of the Investment Sub-Committee and is a trustee of the Carthusian Bursary Trust and the Observer on behalf of the Governing Body of the School for the London Charterhouse charitable body. His non-business interests include the Chairmanship of the British International Harmsworth Trophy, the motorboat equivalent of the Americas Cup, a committee member of the Old Carthusian Yacht Club and is past Chairman of the British Powerboat Racing Club. He lives in Poole in Dorset.
John Olsen, BAJohn Olsen is an Old Carthusian and graduate of Durham University. He has spent his career in corporate reputation management consultancy and now acts as an independent adviser, with a particular focus on the education sector. He served as a Governor of Halstead School for 15 years, including ten as Chair. He has a strong interest in young people’s mental health and wellbeing, and acts as a board advisor to the Charlie Waller Memorial Trust, a leading mental health charity. John is vice chair of the Governing Body and chair of the Nominations and Governance Committee. He additionally sits on the Edgeborough School and Finance and Business Development Committees as well as being a Director of Charterhouse International Ltd.
Mr Royds is a Director at Novatia Financial and Britannicus Stone. He is a graduate of the University of Exeter and is an Old Carthusian. David sits on the Project and Planning Committee and Investment Sub-Committee and is Chair of the Finance and Business Development Committee. David also sits on Charterhouse Enterprises Ltd and Charterhouse School Design and Build Ltd.
Michael Walton, MA, MBA, FRICS
Mr Walton is an Old Malvernian, a graduate of Cambridge University and a postgraduate of City St George’s University. He is a Fellow of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors and a Chartered Member of the Chartered Institute for Securities & Investment. He has spent his career in real estate investment management and has for the last 20 years been Chief Executive of his own business that advises Governments and Institutions on real estate investment throughout Western Europe. He has served as a Governor of Edgeborough School for five years, including three as Chair of the Strategy Development Committee. He attends the School Health and Safety Committee on behalf of the Governing Body and sits on the Committees for Audit, Risk and Compliance, Projects and Planning and Windlesham House School.
The Chair of the Governing Body may be contacted via the Clerk to the Governing Body, Charterhouse, Godalming, Surrey, GU7 2DX. E: clerktogoverningbody@charterhouse.org.uk
The Edgeborough School Sub-Committee meets termly and reports to the Governing Body. Members of the Edgeborough School Committee are: John Olsen (Chair), Durell Barnes, Sarah Hartnell, Caroline Brown (co-opted member), Leanne Rowlands (co-opted member)

Outdoor Woodland Learning (OWL)
Our Forest School inspired, Outdoor Woodland Learning, referred to as OWL, is acclaimed by parents, adored by children and celebrated by teachers. Donning wellies, waterproof and a ‘can do’ sense of adventure, each class (from Pre-School to Year 2) is offered a two hour woodland experience on a weekly basis led by our qualified Forest School Leader.
Within the woodland classroom, the learning potential is immense and the possibility for creativity limitless. Mother nature inspires all learners who will be seen collaborating in projects, developing imaginative themes in play and working with focus on a task. The woods allow for and encourage sensory exploration and therefore a whole-body learning experience. Projects such as constructing hedgehog houses, building mini-beast hotels or planting trees instil in the children a responsibility towards the plant and our school, a welcome message in a world increasingly disconnected from the great outdoors.
Using a range of tools with purpose and being shown how to carry out essential woodland tasks, the children are trusted to carry out ambitious projects. They delight in their success and accomplishments as a result. With the use of saws, peelers, flint lighters and cooking pots around the fire captivating their focus, OWL offers an experience that no classroom can match. Do come and visit our woods, it’s a haven of fun, achievement and enrichment.
Edgeborough School OWL Site backs onto Frensham Forest a significantly important section of the Bourne and Frensham Vale wildlife corridor.

Parents' Association known as Edgeborough Together
Run by parent volunteers, Edgeborough Together strives to promote a strong sense of community through a framework of social events bringing together parents, staff and pupils. At its core, is a focus on the pupils themselves and our events reflect this. Money generated by these events are divided between the School and the School’s charities, which are chosen annually by the children.
The Edgeborough Together Team is made up of Event Co-ordinators, a Treasurer and Representatives from each school year. The Team meets four times a year to discuss and plan events across the School calendar. In addition, the team is available to help welcome and support new families to the School and to provide a central line of communication, keeping all representatives up to date with event information.
Community
Edgeborough Together is a channel of open communication between parents and the School on all matters affecting the wellbeing of the school and the welfare and development of pupils, through our ‘Class Rep’ network.
You are invited to attend Friday Services and are welcomed at a whole host of events throughout the school year. Money is raised for charity with the organisation of a plethora of enjoyable activities.

Pastoral Care
"The children's physical and emotional welfare is at the forefront of everything we do at Edgeborough."
At Edgeborough we are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. Our aim is to provide exceptional pastoral care, embedding a sense of independence, resilience and confidence, where mutual trust and respect between pupils and staff are the fundamental guiding principle, and above all encourage good citizenship.
There is a superb network of support that children can turn to. The child’s first port of call is their form teacher. This is somebody who they see every day and is invested in their welfare. The children have all sorts of other people to choose from if they need something. There are the Heads of Year, the Deputy Heads, Matrons and Gap Teachers. The younger children also sometimes like to talk to the prefects or the Year 8 pupils. In the Boarding House, the children can talk to any of the boarding staff. There is also an independent listener who is very discreet and someone to talk to confidentially, should the occasion arise.
If a child needs some slightly more targeted support, they can speak with an ELSA [Emotional Literacy Support Assistant] or they can see the school counsellor. Our school counsellor works two days a week and appointments can be arranged either directly with the counsellor or via the Deputy Head Pastoral.
We try and make it as easy as we can for children to share a worry or a problem. There is an online pupil communication form that the children can use and send to staff and then the staff can approach them and speak to them about their worry. There is a worry box where children can post their concerns. We also have frequent assemblies where we make children aware of the avenues they can use if they need to.
We have wrap around care where children can take part in breakfast club and late activities and through to boarding should they wish to. The important message we want our children to take away is that they can grow and feel safe and supported in a nurturing environment, with wonderful opportunities along the way. If on occasions there is a bump, we’re there to help them.

Sports
Every boy and girl at Edgeborough enjoys a rich and varied sporting programme. Our sport ethos ensures all pupils play as part of a team, whilst providing opportunities to perform at the highest level of competition.
Sport and activity are an integral part of daily life at Edgeborough.
At Edgeborough we deliver a games programme of core team sports including Rugby, Football, Hockey and Cricket for the boys and Hockey, Netball, Football and Cricket for the girls. Pupils will also represent the school for Swimming, Athletics, Tennis, Judo, Cross Country and Climbing. With a wealth of activities on offer, the children’s enjoyment is well catered for in sport.
This is reflected throughout the school in our PE curriculum; from children in the Nursery taking their first steps towards physical literacy, to a specialist sports programme for Pre-Prep and the Prep learning through co-ed physical Education curriculum. We are very lucky to have our specialist PE staff delivering this from Nursery right through to Year 8.

Tapestry Online Learning Journals
Edgeborough’s Nursery and Pre-Prep Department are excited to be using an online learning journal called Tapestry as a platform to share with you your child’s achievements, progress and success.
Through Tapestry, both practitioners and carers can capture, celebrate and share those moments and milestones of a child’s learning and development. This is done by us and you uploading photographs and providing brief descriptions and comments to describe the action and achievement pictured. Through sharing visual memories of the school day, not only will you get a better understanding of your child’s day and progress but you will be able to sit with them at home and reflect on their week at school as you view Tapestry together. Likewise, when experiences from home are uploaded to the platform, this input will help us at Edgeborough gain a more holistic knowledge of the individual child and their interests, which we can then use to guide our planning and instruction.
